name: Bear Put Diagonal Spread (Long Put Diagonal, Debit)
summary: Buy a longer-dated higher-strike put and sell a shorter-dated lower-strike put; the bearish mirror of the bull call diagonal, financed by repeatedly selling the lower put.

legs.strike_rule: Lower strike by delta |0.25-0.35|, strictly below the long strike, and long strike - short strike >= net debit per share.

max_profit: At the short strike at front expiry: value of the back-month long put there minus the net debit, plus cumulative credits from rolled shorts.
max_loss: The net debit paid, if the underlying rallies far enough that both puts approach zero.
breakevens: Approximately long strike - net debit, adjusted for the long's remaining time value; solve numerically at front expiry.

greeks.delta: net negative, roughly -0.30 to -0.45 per unit
greeks.gamma: slightly negative near the short strike
greeks.theta: positive while spot is above the short strike

when_to_use: Bearish view over 1-3 months on an underlying in a downtrend (spot < 50-day SMA < 200-day SMA), with IV rank 20-50. Note the structural headwind: put skew means the lower-strike short put you sell is relatively more expensive than the call-side equivalent, which helps the financing but also means the short gets tested faster on a drop.
entry_rules: Trend filter: spot < 50-day SMA AND 50-day SMA < 200-day SMA.
IV rank between 20 and 50 (avoid buying the long put after a vol spike).
Long put by delta |0.60-0.75|, 60-120 DTE; short put by delta |0.25-0.35|, 21-45 DTE.
MANDATORY: short strike < long strike, and (long strike - short strike) >= net debit per share.
Short expiry strictly before the long expiry.
Net debit <= 2.5% of equity per unit; combined bid-ask <= 8% of debit.
LEVEL 3 OK: a short put at a LOWER strike expiring EARLIER is fully covered by the long put. Submit as a 2-leg mleg; buy the long put FIRST if legging.
management_rules: Close the short put at 50-75% of the credit received and re-sell the next cycle.
Close the entire structure at +50% of net debit.
Stop at -50% of net debit, or if spot closes above the long strike plus 1 ATR(14).
Trend stop: close if spot closes above the 50-day SMA for 2 consecutive sessions.

Roll the short down and out when spot falls below the short strike and the short's |delta| > 0.60, for a net credit only and only to a strike still below long strike - debit. If no credit roll exists, close the whole diagonal.
Roll the long put forward at DTE < 45 or when its |delta| drops below 0.50.
exit_rules: Close or roll the short put by 14:30 ET on its expiration day, unconditionally.
Close the short put immediately if extrinsic <= $0.05/share or |delta| >= 0.90.
Deep-ITM short puts are exercised early for interest carry - close any short put with extrinsic < $0.10 regardless of DTE.
Close the long put no later than 30 DTE or when |delta| < 0.40.
Buy back the short before selling the long.
If the long put marks below 30% of the entry debit, close both legs.
assignment_risk: Only the short front-month put. Assignment delivers +100 shares at the short strike, consuming strike x 100 of buying power, hedged by a long higher-strike put (effectively a synthetic short via the protective put). Flatten the shares within one session. Early exercise on short puts is rate/carry driven, not dividend driven.
buying_power: Net debit only - the short strike is below the long strike with an earlier expiry, so the long covers it. Assignment temporarily consumes strike x 100.
liquidity_needs: Long leg 60-120 DTE OI >= 200, spread <= $0.20; short leg OI >= 500. Underlying ADV >= 2M shares.
common_mistakes: Selling a short strike too close to the long, so a both-ITM finish loses money; buying the long put after a volatility spike and paying for vega that then collapses; rolling the short for a debit; forgetting that deep-ITM short puts can be assigned early for interest.
zero_dte_notes: Short leg minimum 21 DTE at entry; never carried to 0DTE beyond the 14:30 ET forced close.
family: Calendar and diagonal spreads (time spreads): same-strike calendars, different-strike diagonals, double/triple calendars, double diagonals, PMCC and its put mirror, LEAPS diagonals, calendarized straddles/butterflies, ratio time spreads, and the reverse (short) time spreads
